dropped.item: Joan treated the narrator's fear as a practical problem rather than a character flaw, and the narrator saw this as the kindest thing she could have done
Concrete details of being bad at swimming: clumsy, swallowing water
Watching eight-year-olds glide past in the next lane
The narrator was surprised by how little they minded by the end
Nobody expected the narrator to already know how (the reason the mornings felt restful)
It was the width of the pool the narrator crossed
Closing metaphor of discovering a room in one's own house that had always been there
Instruction to trust that the pool would do part of the work

changed.item: Original says the folded arms might make the narrator 'less visible'. Edit says they are meant to hide how scared she is.
'Bad at it in ways I hadn't been bad at anything in years' became 'as bad ... as I've been bad at anything in my life', which is stronger and has a different scope
'A morning each week' became 'this weekly few hours a week', changing the time commitment
Original presents trusting the pool as an instruction. Edit asserts as fact that 'the pool does take some of my weight'.
'For weeks' became 'For the first few weeks'
Joan's approach is reframed from practical to 'kindness and patience'

added.item: Others, specifically Joan, can see how scared the narrator is ('But they can. Joan can.')
'That's saying a lot' implies a long history of being bad at things

invented_specifics: this weekly few hours a week
